thread:
morgan: heads-up - we saw a tenant get fully evicted after a 90s burst even though their reserve should have covered it. looks like grace-window math is off.
sam: ugh. which policy? reservoir or provisional-lease?
morgan: provisional-lease path. they drained tokens -> soft-evict kicked in, grace window expired during a short network hiccup so eviction completed.
anya: can you paste the request pattern? was it sustained or a single large spike?
morgan: mostly 3x small bursts over 2m, not sustained. logs:
```
2026-03-18T15:02:11Z tenant=acme req=embed size=6
2026-03-18T15:02:12Z tenant=acme req=chat size=120
2026-03-18T15:03:40Z tenant=acme req=chat size=200
```
sam: hmm. current grace-window is fixed 60s after last credit consumption event + drain-probe margin. that margin doesn't account for intermittent network stalls.
kim: i'd rather avoid extending wall-clock grace for everyone — increases abuse surface. maybe make grace window adaptive by recent burstiness score?
anya: agreed. proposal: grace = base + min(max_tail, burst_score * scale). burst_score in [0,1] from probing.
lee: sounds ok but where do we compute burst_score? in admission service or token-steward?
sam: token-steward has access to precise token consumption histogram; cheaper to compute there and emit a header on lease objects. admission/enforcer can read it when evaluating eviction.
morgan: that keeps API boundary clear. token-steward -> lease.burst_score header (0.0-1.0).
anya: we should also ensure behavior for clients with pinned dedicated capacity. they should ignore grace heuristics and follow SLA path.
sam: yes - dedicated tenants flagged exempt in the enforcer config.
kim: quick sketch of config: 
```yaml
provisional_lease:
  base_grace_s: 30
  max_tail_s: 90
  scale: 45  # seconds per burst_score unit
  abuse_threshold: 0.9
```
lee: and runtime pseudocode for enforcer: 
```
if lease.tier == "dedicated": keep_alive
else:
  grace = cfg.base + min(cfg.max_tail, lease.burst_score * cfg.scale)
  if now - last_consumption > grace: start_eviction
```
morgan: need to consider clock skew between services. use monotonic counters or token-timestamp epoch carried on leases.
anya: good point. token-steward can attach last_consumption_epoch (monotonic counter) in the lease. avoids NTP issues.
sam: telemetry: emit eviction_attempt with computed_grace and burst_score. want to be able to slice by tenant, region, model.
devops-bot: deploy/pipeline status: feature-branch=eviction-grace-refactor passed unit tests, behind flag=true. :white_check_mark:
kim: plan: implement in token-steward -> lease metadata, add enforcer read path, add feature flag gate, run canary in us-west-2.
lee: who owns rollout? i can take canary and first metrics dashboard.
morgan: thanks lee. @sam @anya can you pair on the abuse-surface review? esp. how burst_score is derived and if it can be gamed.
anya: will do. quick thought: cap scale so high-burst clients can't get infinite grace. also floor burst_score if detected repeated disconnects.
sam: noted. i'll sketch math and some unit tests.
morgan: ok team — aim to ship behind flag next week and run 72h canary. logging should catch any unexpected early evictions.
lee: +1. i'll add dashboard & alert if eviction rate for non-dedicated rises > 5pct vs baseline. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
morgan: thanks everyone. followups in PR thread.
